---
title: "Shooting responses"
subtitle: "East Alligator"
author: "Scott Forrest"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
execute: 
  cache: false
  warning: false
bibliography: paperpile.bib
toc: true
number-sections: false
format: 
  html:
    self-contained: false
    code-fold: true
    code-summary: "Show code"
    code-tools: true
    df-print: paged
    code-line-numbers: true
    code-overflow: scroll
    fig-format: png
    fig-dpi: 300
  pdf:
    fig-format: png
    fig-dpi: 300
    geometry: 
      - top=30mm
      - left=30mm
editor:
  source
abstract: |
  Here we are looking at how feral pigs respond to aerial shooting operations in the East Alligator region of Kakadu National Park, Northern Territory, Australia. We have GPS tracking data from pigs in the area, and we are looking at how their movement patterns change before and after shooting events. Because the pig's behaviour is temporally variable, we also need to ensure that the timing of the shooting operations isn't correlated with ordinary behavioural changes (which it seems to be). Therefore, as a control, we also run the same analyses on data at the same time of day, but 3 days before shooting occurred, and as an additional control, for pigs that were outside the area shooting was occurring.
  
  We look at changes in their movement behaviour, measured as the distance between successive GPS fixes (step length), as well as their habitat use, measured as the proportion of time they spend in different vegetation classes.
---

# Load packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
packages <- c("amt", "lubridate",
              "terra", "sf",
              "beepr", "tictoc",
              "leaflet", "tidyterra")
walk(packages, require, character.only = T)

```

# Create directories for outputs

```{r}

# general outputs directory
outputs_dir <- "outputs/east_alligator/shooting_responses/"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# for plots with veg categories
outputs_veg_dir <- file.path(outputs_dir, "veg/")
dir.create(outputs_veg_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

```

# Import GPS tracking data

```{r}

pig_all_steps <- read_csv("data/pigs_east_alligator_steps_covs_20261015.csv")

# Convert timezone after import (resets to GMT)
pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% 
  mutate(
    t1_  = with_tz(t1_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin"),
    t2_ = with_tz(t2_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin")
    )

```

## Create sf object of pig data

```{r}

# convert to an sf object (x1_/y1_ are in GDA94 / GA Lambert, EPSG:3112)
# and reproject to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) for leaflet
pig_all_steps_sf <- pig_all_steps %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

```

## Create a bounding box around the pig data to crop the shooting data and other layers by

```{r}

pig_aoi <- st_bbox(pig_all_steps_sf) %>% 
  st_as_sfc() %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 3112) %>% 
  st_buffer(dist = 2500) %>%
  st_bbox() %>% # the buffer creates curved corners so we need to get the bounding box of the buffered area
  st_as_sfc()

# save the bounding box as a shapefile
# pig_aoi %>% 
#   st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
#   st_write("mapping/pig_aoi_wgs84.geojson", driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE)

```

# Shooting data

## Import shooting data from late 2025

In the region where we have pig GPS tracking data, there are two main shooting events. 

```{r}

# Import shapefile of shooting locations using sf - most of the data in East Alligator is actually from late 2025
shooting_locations_2025 <- st_read("mapping/pig_shooting_2026.shp")
# st_crs(shooting_locations_2025)

```

## Import shooting data from 2026

```{r}

shooting_locations_2026 <- read_csv("data/FeralControl_March_Oct2026.csv")

shooting_locations_2026 <- shooting_locations_2026 %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Coordinate_XMin", "Coordinate_YMin"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(shooting_locations_2025))

```

## Plot all of the shooting locations

The late 2025 shooting operations are in red, and the 2026 shooting operations are in blue. The pig GPS locations are coloured by individual.

```{r}

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = pig_all_steps_sf, aes(colour = name), size = 0.1, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = shooting_locations_2025, colour = "red", alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = shooting_locations_2026, colour = "blue", alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

## Combine the two shooting datasets

```{r}

# keep relevant columns
shooting_locations_2025_clean <- shooting_locations_2025 %>% dplyr::select(Time, FeralSpec0, NumberShot, NumberObs0)
shooting_locations_2025_clean <- shooting_locations_2025_clean %>% dplyr::rename("FeralSpecies" = FeralSpec0,
                                                                       "NumberObserved" = NumberObs0)

# keep relevant columns
shooting_locations_2026_clean <- shooting_locations_2026 %>% dplyr::select(Time, FeralSpecies, NumberShot, NumberObserved)

# combine the two datasets
shooting_locations <- bind_rows(shooting_locations_2025_clean, shooting_locations_2026_clean)

```

## Crop the shooting locations to the extent of the pig GPS locations

```{r}

# crop to the extent of the pig GPS locations
filtered_shooting_locations <- shooting_locations %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 3112) %>% 
  st_crop(pig_aoi)

# plot
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = pig_all_steps_sf, aes(colour = name), size = 0.1, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = filtered_shooting_locations, colour = "red", size = 0.5) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

# Overlap between shooting locations and pig GPS locations

## Ensure the timezones match

```{r}

# check the timezone of the pig GPS locations
tz(pig_all_steps_sf$t1_)

# Add a posixct time column to the shooting locations
filtered_shooting_locations <- filtered_shooting_locations %>% mutate(
  shoot_id = row_number(),
  shoot_time = as.POSIXct(Time, format = "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S", tz = "Australia/Darwin")
)

# check the timezone of the shooting locations
tz(filtered_shooting_locations$shoot_time)

# temporal range of the shooting data
min(filtered_shooting_locations$shoot_time)
max(filtered_shooting_locations$shoot_time)

```

## Shooting locations through time

```{r}

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = filtered_shooting_locations, aes(colour = shoot_time), size = 0.5) +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(colour = "Shooting\ntime") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

```

## Timeline of the GPS data collection

The shooting events are shown as the red dashed lines. Each shooting event normally covers several days.

```{r}

ggplot() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = filtered_shooting_locations$shoot_time, 
             colour = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_point(data = pig_all_steps,
             aes(x = t1_, y = name, colour = name),
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + 
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Pig GPS tracking data") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") 

ggsave(paste0(outputs_dir, "pig_shoot_timeline.png"), 
       width = 250, height = 150, units = "mm", scale = 0.75, dpi = 600)

```

### Hours of shooting

```{r}

filtered_shooting_locations <- filtered_shooting_locations %>% 
  mutate(
    shoot_hms = lubridate::hour(shoot_time) + lubridate::minute(shoot_time)/60 + lubridate::second(shoot_time)/3600
  ) 

filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = shoot_hms), bins = 50, fill = "red", colour = "black") +
  scale_x_datetime("Shooting time") +
  theme_bw()

```

### Ensure both objects are in the same coordinate reference system (CRS)

```{r}

# update pig GPS locations to match the CRS of the shooting locations
pig_all_steps_sf <- st_transform(pig_all_steps_sf, st_crs(filtered_shooting_locations))
st_crs(pig_all_steps_sf)$input

```

## Save the filtered shooting locations as a csv

```{r}

filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  mutate(
    x = st_coordinates(.)[, "X"],
    y = st_coordinates(.)[, "Y"]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  write_csv("data/filtered_shooting_locations_3112.csv")

```

## Use leaflet to plot the data

Here we create a plot that can animate the pig GPS locations through time, and show the shooting events as red dots that fade out over a few hours. This helps to visualise the overlap between the pig GPS locations and the shooting events, and to see if there are any obvious changes in pig behaviour after shooting events.

```{r}
#| label: leaflet-map
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# convert to an sf object (x1_/y1_ are in GDA94 / GA Lambert, EPSG:3112)
# and reproject to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) for leaflet
pig_all_steps_sf_wgs84 <- pig_all_steps_sf %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

pal <- colorFactor(viridisLite::viridis(n_distinct(pig_all_steps_sf$name), option = "H"),
                    domain = pig_all_steps_sf$name)

# addCircleMarkers() draws one SVG element per point, and there are ~246k of
# them, which locks up the browser (and the VS Code webview in particular).
# Thin the points for display and draw them with WebGL via leafgl instead.
pig_map_pts <- pig_all_steps_sf_wgs84 %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice(seq(1, n(), by = 1)) %>% # every ith fix per pig
  ungroup()

# Break each pig's track wherever the gap between fixes is longer than this,
# so the lines don't jump across periods with no data
max_gap_hours <- 3

pig_map_pts <- pig_map_pts %>%
  arrange(name, t1_) %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  mutate(new_seg = is.na(lag(t1_)) |
           difftime(t1_, lag(t1_), units = "hours") > max_gap_hours,
         seg = cumsum(new_seg)) %>%
  ungroup()

# one line per pig per continuous run of fixes
pig_map_lines <- pig_map_pts %>%
  group_by(name, seg) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  summarise(do_union = FALSE, .groups = "drop") %>%
  st_cast("LINESTRING")

# Data for the time slider, sorted by time. Coordinates are stored as integers
# (degrees * 1e5, ~1 m) and times as seconds since the first fix, which keeps
# the JSON embedded in the html much smaller
pig_levels <- sort(unique(pig_map_pts$name))
t0 <- min(pig_map_pts$t1_)
pig_time <- pig_map_pts %>% arrange(t1_)
pig_time_xy <- st_coordinates(pig_time)

# Shooting events for the time slider: each appears as a large red dot at its
# shoot_time and fades out over shoot_fade_hours
shoot_fade_hours <- 6
shoot_pts <- filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  filter(!is.na(shoot_time)) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)
shoot_xy <- st_coordinates(shoot_pts)

pig_time_data <- list(
  lng = as.integer(round(pig_time_xy[, "X"] * 1e5)),
  lat = as.integer(round(pig_time_xy[, "Y"] * 1e5)),
  t = as.integer(round(as.numeric(difftime(pig_time$t1_, t0, units = "secs")))),
  pig = match(pig_time$name, pig_levels) - 1L,
  brk = as.integer(pig_time$new_seg),
  pigs = pig_levels,
  cols = pal(pig_levels),
  t0 = as.numeric(t0),
  step = 30 * 60, # slider step (s), matching the 30 min fix rate
  max_gap = max_gap_hours * 3600,
  shoot = list(
    lng = as.integer(round(shoot_xy[, "X"] * 1e5)),
    lat = as.integer(round(shoot_xy[, "Y"] * 1e5)),
    t = as.integer(round(as.numeric(difftime(shoot_pts$shoot_time, t0, units = "secs")))),
    fade = shoot_fade_hours * 3600
  )
)

# The time slider is a custom canvas layer (the leaftime package draws every
# feature as SVG, which has the same problem as addCircleMarkers). Each redraw
# only draws the fixes inside the current time window: the trail of each pig
# as a line plus small points, and its latest fix as a large point (only if
# that fix is within max_gap_hours of the slider time).
pig_time_js <- r"--[
function(el, x, d) {
  var map = this;
  var n = d.t.length, npig = d.pigs.length, STEP = d.step;
  var t = d.t, pig = d.pig, brk = d.brk;
  var lat = new Float64Array(n), lng = new Float64Array(n);
  for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) { lat[i] = d.lat[i] / 1e5; lng[i] = d.lng[i] / 1e5; }
  // htmlwidgets unboxes length-1 vectors, so wrap the shooting columns back
  // into arrays in case there is only one shoot
  var sh = { lat: [].concat(d.shoot.lat), lng: [].concat(d.shoot.lng),
             t: [].concat(d.shoot.t), fade: d.shoot.fade };
  var tMax = Math.ceil(Math.max(t[n - 1], Math.max.apply(null, sh.t)) / STEP) * STEP;
  var state = { cur: 86400, win: 86400, timer: null };

  // first index with t >= v
  function lowerBound(v) {
    var a = 0, b = n;
    while (a < b) { var m = (a + b) >> 1; if (t[m] < v) a = m + 1; else b = m; }
    return a;
  }

  function fmt(s) {
    return new Date((d.t0 + s) * 1000).toLocaleString('en-AU', {
      timeZone: 'Australia/Darwin', day: '2-digit', month: 'short',
      year: 'numeric', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', hour12: false });
  }

  var TimeLayer = L.Layer.extend({
    onAdd: function(m) {
      this._canvas = L.DomUtil.create('canvas', 'leaflet-zoom-hide');
      this._canvas.style.pointerEvents = 'none';
      m.getPanes().overlayPane.appendChild(this._canvas);
      m.on('moveend resize', this._reset, this);
      this._reset();
    },
    onRemove: function(m) {
      L.DomUtil.remove(this._canvas);
      m.off('moveend resize', this._reset, this);
    },
    _reset: function() {
      var size = map.getSize(), r = window.devicePixelRatio || 1, c = this._canvas;
      L.DomUtil.setPosition(c, map.containerPointToLayerPoint([0, 0]));
      c.width = size.x * r; c.height = size.y * r;
      c.style.width = size.x + 'px'; c.style.height = size.y + 'px';
      this.redraw();
    },
    redraw: function() {
      var c = this._canvas, ctx = c.getContext('2d'), r = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
      ctx.setTransform(r, 0, 0, r, 0, 0);
      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, c.width / r, c.height / r);

      var lo = lowerBound(state.cur - state.win), hi = lowerBound(state.cur + 1);
      var px = new Float32Array(hi - lo), py = new Float32Array(hi - lo);
      var byPig = [], i, j, k, q, idx;
      for (k = 0; k < npig; k++) byPig.push([]);
      for (i = lo; i < hi; i++) {
        var p = map.latLngToContainerPoint([lat[i], lng[i]]);
        px[i - lo] = p.x; py[i - lo] = p.y;
        byPig[pig[i]].push(i);
      }

      ctx.lineWidth = 1.5; ctx.lineJoin = 'round';
      for (k = 0; k < npig; k++) {
        idx = byPig[k];
        if (!idx.length) continue;
        ctx.strokeStyle = d.cols[k]; ctx.fillStyle = d.cols[k];
        ctx.globalAlpha = 0.7;
        ctx.beginPath();
        for (j = 0; j < idx.length; j++) {
          q = idx[j] - lo;
          if (j === 0 || brk[idx[j]]) ctx.moveTo(px[q], py[q]); else ctx.lineTo(px[q], py[q]);
        }
        ctx.stroke();
        ctx.globalAlpha = 0.6;
        ctx.beginPath();
        for (j = 0; j < idx.length; j++) {
          q = idx[j] - lo;
          ctx.moveTo(px[q] + 2.5, py[q]); ctx.arc(px[q], py[q], 2.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
        }
        ctx.fill();
      }

      ctx.globalAlpha = 1; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.strokeStyle = '#fff';
      for (k = 0; k < npig; k++) {
        idx = byPig[k];
        if (!idx.length) continue;
        i = idx[idx.length - 1];
        if (state.cur - t[i] > d.max_gap) continue;
        q = i - lo;
        ctx.fillStyle = d.cols[k];
        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(px[q], py[q], 6, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
        ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
      }

      // shooting events: full opacity at shoot_time, fading linearly to zero
      // over sh.fade seconds
      ctx.fillStyle = '#e60000';
      for (i = 0; i < sh.t.length; i++) {
        var age = state.cur - sh.t[i];
        if (age < 0 || age > sh.fade) continue;
        var s = map.latLngToContainerPoint([sh.lat[i] / 1e5, sh.lng[i] / 1e5]);
        ctx.globalAlpha = 1 - age / sh.fade;
        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(s.x, s.y, 10, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
        ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
      }
      ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
    }
  });

  var layer = new TimeLayer().addTo(map);

  var ctrl = L.control({ position: 'bottomleft' });
  ctrl.onAdd = function() {
    var div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'leaflet-bar');
    div.style.cssText = 'background:#fff;padding:6px 10px;font:12px/1.5 sans-serif;';
    div.innerHTML =
      '<div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px">' +
        '<button type="button" class="pt-play" style="width:30px">&#9654;</button>' +
        '<button type="button" class="pt-back" title="Back 30 min">&#8249;</button>' +
        '<div style="width:420px">' +
          '<input type="range" class="pt-slider" min="0" max="' + tMax + '" step="' + STEP +
            '" value="' + state.cur + '" style="width:100%;margin:0;display:block">' +
          // strip of shooting ticks under the slider; the side margins
          // roughly match the inset of the slider thumb's travel
          '<div class="pt-shoots" title="Click to jump to the nearest shooting event"' +
            ' style="position:relative;height:9px;margin:1px 8px 0;cursor:pointer"></div>' +
        '</div>' +
        '<button type="button" class="pt-fwd" title="Forward 30 min">&#8250;</button>' +
      '</div>' +
      '<div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;margin-top:4px">' +
        '<span class="pt-label" style="min-width:290px"></span>' +
        'Trail <select class="pt-win">' +
          '<option value="21600">6 hours</option>' +
          '<option value="86400" selected>1 day</option>' +
          '<option value="259200">3 days</option>' +
          '<option value="604800">1 week</option>' +
          '<option value="2592000">30 days</option>' +
          '<option value="Infinity">All to date</option>' +
        '</select>' +
        'Speed <select class="pt-speed">' +
          '<option value="1800">30 min/s</option>' +
          '<option value="3600">1 hour/s</option>' +
          '<option value="10800">3 hours/s</option>' +
          '<option value="21600">6 hours/s</option>' +
          '<option value="43200">12 hours/s</option>' +
          '<option value="86400" selected>1 day/s</option>' +
          '<option value="259200">3 days/s</option>' +
          '<option value="604800">1 week/s</option>' +
        '</select>' +
      '</div>';
    L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div);
    L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(div);
    return div;
  };
  ctrl.addTo(map);

  var div = ctrl.getContainer();
  var slider = div.querySelector('.pt-slider'), label = div.querySelector('.pt-label');
  var playBtn = div.querySelector('.pt-play'), win = div.querySelector('.pt-win');
  var speed = div.querySelector('.pt-speed');

  function update() {
    slider.value = state.cur;
    label.textContent = fmt(Math.max(0, state.cur - state.win)) + '  –  ' + fmt(state.cur);
    layer.redraw();
  }
  function stop() {
    clearInterval(state.timer); state.timer = null; playBtn.innerHTML = '&#9654;';
  }

  // Playback speed is in seconds of data per real second. Each tick advances a
  // whole number of slider steps, with at most 10 ticks per second, so slow
  // speeds tick less often rather than moving by part of a step
  function start() {
    var rate = Number(speed.value);
    var k = Math.max(1, Math.round(rate / 10 / STEP));
    state.timer = setInterval(function() {
      state.cur = Math.min(state.cur + k * STEP, tMax);
      update();
      if (state.cur >= tMax) stop();
    }, 1000 * k * STEP / rate);
  }
  function stepBy(nSteps) {
    state.cur = Math.min(Math.max(state.cur + nSteps * STEP, 0), tMax);
    update();
  }

  // One red tick per slider step that has a shooting event in it. Clicking
  // the strip jumps to the nearest event, rounded up to the slider step so
  // the shooting dot is drawn at full opacity
  var shootBar = div.querySelector('.pt-shoots');
  var shootSteps = sh.t.map(function(s) {
    return Math.min(Math.max(Math.ceil(s / STEP) * STEP, 0), tMax);
  }).filter(function(s, i, a) { return a.indexOf(s) === i; })
    .sort(function(a, b) { return a - b; });
  shootSteps.forEach(function(s) {
    var tick = document.createElement('div');
    tick.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;top:0;width:2px;height:9px;margin-left:-1px;' +
      'background:#e60000;pointer-events:none;left:' + (100 * s / tMax) + '%';
    shootBar.appendChild(tick);
  });
  shootBar.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
    if (!shootSteps.length) return;
    var box = shootBar.getBoundingClientRect();
    var tClick = (e.clientX - box.left) / box.width * tMax;
    var best = shootSteps[0];
    shootSteps.forEach(function(s) {
      if (Math.abs(s - tClick) < Math.abs(best - tClick)) best = s;
    });
    stop();
    state.cur = best;
    update();
  });

  slider.addEventListener('input', function() { state.cur = +slider.value; update(); });
  win.addEventListener('change', function() { state.win = Number(win.value); update(); });
  speed.addEventListener('change', function() {
    if (state.timer) { clearInterval(state.timer); start(); }
  });
  div.querySelector('.pt-back').addEventListener('click', function() { stepBy(-1); });
  div.querySelector('.pt-fwd').addEventListener('click', function() { stepBy(1); });
  playBtn.addEventListener('click', function() {
    if (state.timer) { stop(); return; }
    if (state.cur >= tMax) state.cur = 0;
    playBtn.innerHTML = '&#10074;&#10074;';
    start();
  });

  update();
}
]--"

pig_map <- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
  leafgl::addGlPolylines(data = pig_map_lines,
                         color = pal(pig_map_lines$name),
                         opacity = 0.6,
                         weight = 1.5,
                         group = "All tracks") %>%
  leafgl::addGlPoints(data = pig_map_pts,
                      fillColor = pal(pig_map_pts$name),
                      fillOpacity = 0.75,
                      radius = 5,
                      popup = paste0("ID: ", pig_map_pts$name,
                                     "<br>Time: ", pig_map_pts$t1_),
                      group = "All fixes") %>%
  addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal,
            values = pig_map_pts$name, title = "Pig ID") %>%
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft",
              options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE)) %>%
  addLegend(position = "bottomright", colors = "#e60000",
            labels = paste0("Shooting (fades over ", shoot_fade_hours, " h)")) %>%
  # the full tracks and fixes are off by default so the time slider layer is
  # readable; tick them on in the layers control
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("All tracks", "All fixes"),
                   options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) %>%
  hideGroup(c("All tracks", "All fixes")) %>%
  htmlwidgets::onRender(pig_time_js, data = pig_time_data)

# The VS Code htmlwidget viewer struggles with large maps, so when working
# interactively write the map out and open it in the system browser. When the
# document is rendered, the widget is printed inline as usual.
if (interactive()) {
  map_file <- file.path("outputs", "pig_map.html") #tempdir()
  # selfcontained = FALSE writes a sibling _files/ folder, which avoids needing
  # pandoc on the path and is much faster to write for a map this size
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(pig_map, map_file, selfcontained = TRUE)
  utils::browseURL(map_file)
} else {
  pig_map
}

```

## Distance in time and space of pig GPS locations to shooting events

```{r}

# find all pig/shooting pairs within x m (returns a list of indices)
# this is irrespective of time at this point
idx <- st_is_within_distance(pig_all_steps_sf, filtered_shooting_locations, dist = 500)

# turn that into a table of matched pairs
# this means that this pig GPS location is within x m of this shooting location
pairs <- tibble(
  pig_row   = rep(seq_along(idx), lengths(idx)),
  shoot_row = unlist(idx)
)

# distance between pig GPS points and shooting locations in metres
pairs$dist_m <- as.numeric(
  st_distance(pig_all_steps_sf[pairs$pig_row, ],
              filtered_shooting_locations[pairs$shoot_row, ],
              by_element = TRUE)
)

# attach the attributes from both objects
hits <- bind_cols(
  # keep only the GPS locations that are within x m of a shooting location
  pig_all_steps_sf[pairs$pig_row, ],
  filtered_shooting_locations[pairs$shoot_row, ] %>% st_drop_geometry(), #%>% rename_with(~ paste0("shoot_", .x)),
  dist_m = pairs$dist_m
)

# keep only the GPS locations that are within 3 hours of a shooting event
# also add the time difference between the pig GPS location and the shooting event (in hours)
# negative values are before the shooting event, positive values are after 
hits <- hits %>% 
  filter(t1_ >= shoot_time - hours(3),
         t1_ <= shoot_time + hours(3)) %>% 
  mutate(
    shoot_time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours")),
  ) 

```

### Keep only the nearest in time

For each shooting location and each pig, take the pig GPS location that is nearest in time to the shooting event.

For instance, within 3 hours either side of the shooting times, we have 182 instances where a pig was within 2000 m of a shooting event. What we have left in this dataframe is the 'focal shooting location', meaning it was nearest in time to the shooting event for that pig. 

Using the focal shooting location, we will extract a sequence of locations from before and after the shooting event, to see if there is a change in behaviour.

```{r}
  
hits_nearest_time <- hits %>% 
  group_by(name, shoot_id) %>% 
  slice_min(abs(shoot_time_diff), n = 1)  %>% 
  ungroup()

hits_nearest_time

# there are four periods with a couple days of shooting
ggplot(hits_nearest_time, aes(x = shoot_time)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "red", colour = "black") +
  scale_x_datetime("Time difference between pig GPS location and shooting event (hours)") +
  theme_bw()

```

### Extract pig GPS locations either side of the focal shoot location

```{r}

shoot_focal_window <- 24 # time either side of focal shooting location (in hours)

# one row per pig/shooting instance, with the temporal window to filter the data by
focal <- hits_nearest_time %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  distinct(name, shoot_id, shoot_time) %>%
  mutate(win_start = shoot_time - hours(shoot_focal_window),
         win_end   = shoot_time + hours(shoot_focal_window))

# shooting locations, one row per shoot_id
shoot_geom <- filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  select(shoot_id)

# distance (m) from each fix to the pig's own GPS fix nearest in time to the shoot
# (i.e. where the pig was at t = 0), so every sequence starts from 0 at the shoot.
# Staying near 0 after the shoot suggests bunkering down, rapid increases suggest fleeing
add_dist_to_t0 <- function(seqs) {
  seqs %>%
    group_by(seq_id) %>%
    mutate(
      dist_to_t0_m = as.numeric(
        st_distance(geometry, geometry[which.min(abs(time_diff_hrs))]))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# pull every GPS fix for that pig inside the window
shooting_sequences <- pig_all_steps_sf %>%
  inner_join(focal,
             by = join_by(name, between(t1_, win_start, win_end)),
             relationship = "many-to-many")

# distance (m) from each fix to its own focal shooting location
shooting_sequences <- shooting_sequences %>%
  mutate(
    dist_to_shoot_m = as.numeric(
      st_distance(geometry,
                  shoot_geom$geometry[match(shoot_id, shoot_geom$shoot_id)],
                  by_element = TRUE)),
    time_diff_hrs = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours")),
    period = if_else(time_diff_hrs < 0, "baseline", "response"),
    seq_id = paste(name, shoot_id, sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  arrange(seq_id, t1_) %>%
  add_dist_to_t0()

head(shooting_sequences, 10) # printing every row bloats the rendered html

```

### Just use the first matching shoot of each day

Often, there are multiple shooting locations on the same day - we will therefore only look at the first shooting event for each pig on that day, and the GPS locations either side of that event.

```{r}

shooting_sequences_daily <- shooting_sequences %>% 
  mutate(
    shoot_date = lubridate::as_date(shoot_time)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(name, shoot_date) %>% 
  slice_min(shoot_time, n = 1)  %>% 
  ungroup()

head(shooting_sequences_daily, 10)

```

# Pig responses to shooting events

## Distance to the shooting location

Here we are looking at the distance of the pig GPS locations to the shooting location, relative to the time of the shooting event. The red dashed line is the time of the shooting event. Larger values mean they are further away, meaning that increasing values show that they are moving away from where the shooting happened. 

```{r}

shooting_sequences_daily %>%        
  ggplot(aes(x = time_diff_hrs, y = dist_to_shoot_m, colour = seq_id)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_path(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous("Distance to the shooting location (m)") +
  labs(title = "Observed shooting events") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

## Distance from the pig's location at the time of shooting

Here the distance is measured from each pig's own GPS location nearest in time to the shooting event, so every sequence is 0 at t = 0. Values that stay near 0 after the shoot suggest the pig bunkered down, and values that increase rapidly suggest it fled.

```{r}

shooting_sequences_daily %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time_diff_hrs, y = dist_to_t0_m, colour = seq_id)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_path(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous("Distance from location at time of shooting (m)") +
  labs(title = "Observed shooting events") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

## Distance between GPS locations

We call the distance between successive GPS locations the 'step length' (sl). Here we are looking at the step lengths of the pig GPS locations relative to the time of the shooting event. The red dashed line is the time of the shooting event. Larger values mean they are moving faster.

The GPS locations were set to record locations every half an hour, so the step lengths are (typically, sometimes there are missing fixes) the distance between locations every half an hour.

```{r}

bin_width <- 0.5  # hours

bin_means <- shooting_sequences_daily %>%
  mutate(bin = floor(time_diff_hrs / bin_width) * bin_width + bin_width / 2) %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_sl = mean(sl_, na.rm = TRUE),
    se      = sd(sl_, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(sl_))),
    q25     = quantile(sl_, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q50     = quantile(sl_, probs = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75     = quantile(sl_, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    n       = sum(!is.na(sl_)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

shooting_sequences_daily %>% #filter(name == "Dora the Explorer") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time_diff_hrs, y = sl_, colour = seq_id)) +
  geom_path(alpha = 0.25) +
  
  # mean with error bar
  # geom_errorbar(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
  #               aes(x = bin, ymin = mean_sl - se, ymax = mean_sl + se),
  #               width = bin_width * 0.3) +
  # geom_line(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
  #           aes(x = bin, y = mean_sl), colour = "black") +
  # geom_point(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
  #            aes(x = bin, y = mean_sl), colour = "black", size = 2) +
  
  # median and quartiles
  geom_line(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = bin, y = q25), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = bin, y = q50), colour = "black") +
  geom_line(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = bin, y = q75), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(x = bin, y = q50), colour = "black", size = 2) +
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  scale_y_continuous("Step length (m)") +
  scale_x_continuous("GPS time relative to shooting event (hours)", 
                     breaks = seq(-shoot_focal_window, shoot_focal_window, by = 3)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 750)) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  labs(title = "Observed shooting events") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") 

# hist(lubridate::hour(shooting_sequences_daily$shoot_time))

```

# Create control sets of responses

## 5 days before each shooting operation

Given the fairly consistent time of shooting operations (in the morning), we don't know whether the behavioural patterns that we are observing are due to the shooting or just their typical behaviour for those times of day.

For this, we will generate a control for comparison. Given that each of the shooting events covered a couple days, we will take sequences of locations from the pigs that were exposed to shooting, at the same time of day as each of the shooting events, but 5 days before the actual shooting events.

We run essentially the same code, but just subtract 5 days from the sequences that we use to extract locations.

```{r}

pseudo_interval <- lubridate::days(5)

# One row per focal pig/shooting event, with the temporal window
focal_pseudo <- hits_nearest_time %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  distinct(name, shoot_id, shoot_time) %>%
  mutate(
    shoot_time = shoot_time - pseudo_interval,
    win_start = shoot_time - hours(shoot_focal_window),
    win_end   = shoot_time + hours(shoot_focal_window)
    )

# Shooting locations, same CRS as the pigs, one row per shoot_id
shoot_geom <- filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  select(shoot_id)

# Pull every GPS fix for that pig inside the window
seqs_pseudo <- pig_all_steps_sf %>% 
  inner_join(focal_pseudo,
             by = join_by(name, between(t1_, win_start, win_end)),
             relationship = "many-to-many")

# Distance (m) from each fix to its own focal shooting location
seqs_pseudo <- seqs_pseudo %>%
  mutate(
    dist_to_shoot_m = as.numeric(
      st_distance(geometry,
                  shoot_geom$geometry[match(shoot_id, shoot_geom$shoot_id)],
                  by_element = TRUE)),
    time_diff_hrs = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours")),
    period = if_else(time_diff_hrs < 0, "baseline", "response"),
    seq_id = paste(name, shoot_id, sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  arrange(seq_id, t1_) %>%
  add_dist_to_t0()

head(seqs_pseudo, 10)

```

### Just use the first matching shoot of each day

There are multiple shooting locations on the same day - we will therefore only look at the first shooting event for each pig on that day, and the GPS locations either side of that event.

```{r}

shooting_sequences_daily_pseudo <- seqs_pseudo %>% 
  mutate(
    shoot_date = lubridate::as_date(shoot_time)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(name, shoot_date) %>% 
  slice_min(shoot_time, n = 1)  %>% 
  ungroup()

head(shooting_sequences_daily_pseudo, 10)
```

## Same time but far away

Here we get locations for pigs that have locations at the same time as the shooting events, but which were more than 5 km away.

```{r}

shoot_distance <- 10000  # metres

# add an ID to the shooting locations
shoot <- filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  mutate(shoot_id = row_number())

# add an ID to the pig GPS locations
pig <- pig_all_steps_sf %>%
  mutate(pig_row = row_number())

# initial matching window - just grab the pig locations that are 
# within three hours of the shooting locations
window <- 3 * 3600  # seconds; narrow this if you want "same time" more strictly

# time-match pairs 
pairs <- pig %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(name, pig_row, t1_) %>%                        # your pig timestamp column
  inner_join(
    shoot %>%
      st_drop_geometry() %>%
      transmute(shoot_id, shoot_time,          # your shooting timestamp column
                lo = shoot_time - window,
                hi = shoot_time + window),
    by = join_by(between(t1_, lo, hi))
  )

# distance for each matched pair only
pairs$dist_m <- st_distance(
  st_geometry(pig)[pairs$pig_row],
  st_geometry(shoot)[pairs$shoot_id],
  by_element = TRUE
) %>% as.numeric()

hist(pairs$dist_m)

# fixes more than 10 km from a shooting event while it was happening
far_during_shooting <- pairs %>%
  filter(dist_m > shoot_distance) %>% 
  mutate(
    shoot_time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours"))
  )

# keep only the nearest in time
hits_nearest_time_far <- far_during_shooting %>% 
  group_by(name, shoot_id) %>% 
  slice_min(abs(shoot_time_diff), n = 1)  %>% 
  ungroup()

# pull out the shoot ids that had matching locations
obs_shoot_ids <- unique(hits_nearest_time$shoot_id)

# keep the far away locations for shoot ids where there was overlap
hits_nearest_time_far <- hits_nearest_time_far %>% filter(shoot_id %in% obs_shoot_ids)

```

# Compare the observed and control responses together

## Combine the data frames

```{r}

shooting_sequences_daily_all <- shooting_sequences_daily %>% 
  mutate(type = "Observed") %>% 
  bind_rows(shooting_sequences_daily_pseudo %>% mutate(type = "Pseudo")) %>% 
  bind_rows(shooting_sequences_daily_far %>% mutate(type = "Far"))

# setting the colours for the shooting
shoot_cols <- c("Observed" = "#D55E00",   # vermillion
                "Far"      = "#0072B2",   # blue
                "Pseudo"   = "#009E73")   # bluish green

shoot_labels <- c("Observed" = "Observed shoots",
                  "Far"      = "Far from shoots",
                  "Pseudo"   = "5 days before")

```

## Distance from the location at the time of shooting

Median (line) and interquartile range (ribbon) of the distance from each pig's location at the time of shooting. A curve that stays flat near 0 after the shoot indicates bunkering down, and a steeper rise for the observed shoots than for the controls indicates fleeing.

```{r}
#| results: asis

bin_width <- 0.5  # hours

# date windows of each shooting operation (same as the step length plots below)
shoot_operations <- tribble(
  ~op,                                      ~file_suffix, ~window_min,           ~window_max,
  "All shooting operations",                "all",        as_date("2025 01 01"), as_date("2027 01 01"),
  "First shoot (early Nov 2025)",           "first",      as_date("2025 11 01"), as_date("2025 11 10"),
  "Second shoot (late Nov/early Dec 2025)", "second",     as_date("2025 11 20"), as_date("2025 12 14"),
  "Third shoot (May 2026)",                 "third",      as_date("2026 05 12"), as_date("2026 05 30"),
  "Fourth shoot (Aug 2026)",                "fourth",     as_date("2026 08 12"), as_date("2026 08 30")
)

cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(shoot_operations))) {

  op_i <- shoot_operations[i, ]

  dist_t0_bins <- shooting_sequences_daily_all %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(shoot_time > op_i$window_min & shoot_time < op_i$window_max) %>%
    mutate(bin = floor(time_diff_hrs / bin_width) * bin_width + bin_width / 2) %>%
    group_by(type, bin) %>%
    summarise(
      q25 = quantile(dist_to_t0_m, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q50 = quantile(dist_to_t0_m, probs = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
      q75 = quantile(dist_to_t0_m, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      n   = sum(!is.na(dist_to_t0_m)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  p <- dist_t0_bins %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = bin)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75, fill = type),
                alpha = 0.25, colour = alpha("black", 0.75), linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_line(aes(y = q50, colour = type)) +
    geom_point(aes(y = q50, colour = type), size = 1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    scale_y_continuous("Distance from location at time of shooting (m)") +
    scale_x_continuous("GPS time relative to shooting event (hours)",
                       breaks = seq(-shoot_focal_window, shoot_focal_window, by = 3)) +
```

:::

# Vegetation responses

Here we are looking at whether the pigs changed the habitat that they were in either side of the shooting events. I.e. did they switch from a more open habitat to a more closed habitat for shelter/safety.

### Define colours for the vegetation classes

```{r}

veg_colours <- c(
  "Dry Rainforest"          = "#1B5E3A",  # dark green
  "Eucalypt Open Forest"    = "#B5772B",  # deep ochre
  "Eucalypt Woodland"       = "#E0B65C",  # light ochre
  "Floodplain Sedgeland"    = "#D6E2A3",  # pale yellow-green
  "Melaleuca Woodland"      = "#A9CCE3",  # light blue
  "Melaleuca Open Forest"   = "#5B97BF",  # mid blue
  "Melaleuca Closed Forest" = "#2B5F8A",  # dark blue
  "Mangrove"                = "#2A9D8F",  # teal
  "Mudflat"                 = "#8A7968",  # grey-brown
  "Water"                   = "#264653"   # dark blue-gray"
)

```

### Proportions of vegetation classes either side of the shooting events

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 8

bin_width <- 0.5  # hours

cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(shoot_operations))) {

  op_i <- shoot_operations[i, ]

  # proportion of each class per time bin, separately for the observed and control sequences
  veg_props_shoot <- shooting_sequences_daily_all %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(shoot_time > op_i$window_min & shoot_time < op_i$window_max,
           !is.na(Veg_class)) %>%
    mutate(bin = floor(time_diff_hrs / bin_width) * bin_width + bin_width / 2) %>%
    count(type, bin, Veg_class) %>%
    # fill classes that weren't used in a bin with zeros so the areas stack properly
    complete(type, bin, Veg_class, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    group_by(type, bin) %>%
    mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.nan(prop)) %>%
    mutate(type = factor(type, levels = names(shoot_labels), labels = shoot_labels),
           Veg_class = factor(Veg_class, levels = names(veg_colours)))

  p <- veg_props_shoot %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = bin, y = prop, fill = Veg_class)) +
    geom_area(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +

    # add a line for the time of the shooting event
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +

    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_x_continuous("GPS time relative to shooting event (hours)",
                       breaks = seq(-shoot_focal_window, shoot_focal_window, by = 3),
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = "Vegetation use either side of the shooting events", subtitle = op_i$op,
         y = "Proportion of steps", fill = "Vegetation class") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = veg_colours, drop = TRUE) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    facet_wrap(~ type, ncol = 1) +
    theme_bw()

  ggsave(file.path(outputs_veg_dir, paste0("veg_props_shooting_vs_pseudo_", op_i$file_suffix, ".png")),
         plot = p, width = 150, height = 180, scale = 1.25, units = "mm", dpi = 600)

  # one tab per shooting operation: heading first, then the plot
  cat("\n\n#### ", op_i$op, "\n\n")
  print(p)
}

cat("\n\n:::\n")

```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## All shooting operations

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

bin_width <- 0.5  # hours
z <- qnorm(0.975) # 95% interval

seqs_win <- shooting_sequences_daily_all %>%
  mutate(bin = floor(time_diff_hrs / bin_width) * bin_width + bin_width / 2)

veg_cols <- grep("^veg_", names(seqs_win), value = TRUE)

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)

cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")

for (veg_col in veg_cols) {

  veg_label <- gsub("_", " ", sub("^veg_", "", veg_col)) %>%
    stringr::str_to_sentence()

  bin_summary <- seqs_win %>%
    group_by(type, bin) %>%
    summarise(
      n = sum(!is.na(.data[[veg_col]])),
      k = sum(.data[[veg_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(n > 0) %>%
    mutate(
      p      = k / n,
      centre = (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / (1 + z^2 / n),
      half   = z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / (1 + z^2 / n),
      lower  = pmax(0, centre - half),
      upper  = pmin(1, centre + half)
    )

  p <- ggplot(bin_summary, aes(x = bin, colour = type, fill = type, group = type)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                alpha = 0.25, colour = alpha("black", 0.75), linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_line(aes(y = p)) +
    geom_point(aes(y = p), size = 1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    scale_y_continuous("Proportion of fixes",
                       limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    scale_x_continuous("GPS time relative to shooting event (hours)",
                       breaks = seq(-shoot_focal_window, shoot_focal_window, by = 3)) + 
    scale_colour_manual(name = "Shoot vs\ncontrol", values = shoot_cols, labels = shoot_labels) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Shoot vs\ncontrol", values = shoot_cols, labels = shoot_labels) +
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = veg_label,
         subtitle = "All shooting operations",
         colour = "Shoot", fill = "Shoot") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  ggsave(file.path(outputs_veg_dir, paste0(veg_col, "_shooting_vs_pseudo_all.png")),
         plot = p, width = 150, height = 100, units = "mm", dpi = 600)

  # one tab per habitat: heading first, then the plot
  cat("\n\n#### ", veg_label, "\n\n")
  print(p)
}

cat("\n\n:::\n")

```

```{r}
      lower  = pmax(0, centre - half),
      upper  = pmin(1, centre + half)
    )

  p <- ggplot(bin_summary, aes(x = bin, colour = type, fill = type, group = type)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                alpha = 0.25, colour = alpha("black", 0.75), linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_line(aes(y = p)) +
    geom_point(aes(y = p), size = 1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    scale_y_continuous("Proportion of fixes",
                       limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    scale_x_continuous("GPS time relative to shooting event (hours)",
                       breaks = seq(-shoot_focal_window, shoot_focal_window, by = 3)) +
    scale_colour_manual(name = "Shoot vs\ncontrol", values = shoot_cols, labels = shoot_labels) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = "Shoot vs\ncontrol", values = shoot_cols, labels = shoot_labels) +
    labs(title = veg_label,
         subtitle = "Second shooting operations: 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-01",
         colour = "Shoot", fill = "Shoot") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  ggsave(file.path(outputs_veg_dir, paste0(veg_col, "_shooting_vs_pseudo_second.png")),
         plot = p, width = 150, height = 100, units = "mm", dpi = 600)

  # one tab per habitat: heading first, then the plot
  cat("\n\n#### ", veg_label, "\n\n")
  print(p)
}

cat("\n\n:::\n")

```

# Paired comparisons: observed shoots vs 5 days before

The 5-days-before control uses the same pig at the same time of day (and likely in a similar area), so each observed sequence can be paired with its own control sequence (matched by `seq_id`, i.e. pig × shoot). For each pair we:

1. summarise each metric within fixed time windows relative to the shoot (one value per sequence per window),
2. subtract the 5-days-before value from the observed value (observed − control), and
3. test whether those paired differences are centred on 0 using a Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

Pairing cancels out the diel cycle and differences between individual pigs, and summarising to one value per pair and window avoids treating the autocorrelated 30-minute fixes as independent. The histograms show exactly what each test is assessing: the distribution of paired differences, with the dashed line at 0 (no difference) and the solid line at the median difference. A shift of the histogram away from 0 is what the test detects.

A few caveats: there are only a small number of pairs, and some pigs contribute more than one pair, so the pairs are not fully independent (a mixed model with a random intercept for pig would account for this). We report p-values adjusted for multiple testing (Benjamini–Hochberg, within each metric) alongside the raw values.

## Set up the paired data

```{r}

# time windows (hours relative to the shoot) for the paired comparisons
# windows include their start and exclude their end, so the fix at t = 0 is in the first window after the shoot
paired_breaks <- c(-3, 0, 3, 6, 12, 24)
paired_labels <- c("3-0 h before", "0-3 h after", "3-6 h after", "6-12 h after", "12-24 h after")

paired_data <- shooting_sequences_daily_all %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(type %in% c("Observed", "Pseudo")) %>%
  mutate(window = cut(time_diff_hrs, breaks = paired_breaks, labels = paired_labels, right = FALSE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(window))

# number of sequences that have both an observed and a control sequence
paired_data %>%
  distinct(type, seq_id) %>%
  count(type)

# Wilcoxon signed-rank test of whether the paired differences are centred on 0,
# with Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values across all the tests in the table
paired_wilcox <- function(diffs, ...) {
  diffs %>%
    group_by(...) %>%
    summarise(
      n           = sum(!is.na(diff)),
      median_diff = median(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_diff   = mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
      # returns NA when all differences are 0 (e.g. a vegetation class that was never used)
      p_value     = if (all(diff == 0, na.rm = TRUE)) NA_real_ else
                      suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(diff, mu = 0, exact = FALSE)$p.value),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))
}

# histogram of the paired differences, with 0 (dashed) and the median difference (solid)
plot_paired_diffs <- function(diffs, tests, x_lab, title, digits = 2) {

  tests <- tests %>%
    mutate(label = paste0("n = ", n,
                          "\nmean = ", round(mean_diff, digits),
                          "\np = ", signif(p_value, 2),
                          "\np adj = ", signif(p_adj, 2)))

  diffs %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = diff)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = shoot_cols["Observed"], colour = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_rug(colour = shoot_cols["Observed"], alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(data = tests, aes(xintercept = mean_diff), colour = shoot_cols["Observed"], linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = tests, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
              hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.1, size = 2.5, lineheight = 0.9) +
    scale_y_continuous("Number of pairs", expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.6))) +
    labs(x = x_lab, title = title,
         subtitle = "Observed shoot minus the same pig 5 days before") +
    theme_bw()
}

```

## Distance from the location at the time of shooting

Mean distance (m) from the pig's location at t = 0 within each window. Positive differences mean the pig was further from where it was at t = 0 on the shoot day than at the same time 5 days before (i.e. fleeing), and differences near 0 mean no change relative to normal movement.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

dist_t0_diffs <- paired_data %>%
  group_by(type, seq_id, name, window) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(dist_to_t0_m, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(diff = Observed - Pseudo) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff))

dist_t0_tests <- paired_wilcox(dist_t0_diffs, window)
dist_t0_tests

plot_paired_diffs(dist_t0_diffs, dist_t0_tests,
                  x_lab = "Difference in mean distance from location at time of shooting (m)",
                  title = "Distance from the location at the time of shooting",
                  digits = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ window, nrow = 1)

ggsave(paste0(outputs_dir, "paired_diff_dist_to_t0.png"),
       width = 250, height = 90, units = "mm", scale = 1, dpi = 600)

write_csv(dist_t0_tests, paste0(outputs_dir, "paired_tests_dist_to_t0.csv"))

```

## Step lengths

Mean log(step length + 1) within each window. Differences are on the log scale, so `exp(diff)` is the ratio of the (geometric mean) step lengths, e.g. a difference of 0.69 means steps were about twice as long on the shoot day as 5 days before.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

sl_diffs <- paired_data %>%
  group_by(type, seq_id, name, window) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(log1p(sl_), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(diff = Observed - Pseudo) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff))

sl_tests <- paired_wilcox(sl_diffs, window) %>%
  mutate(median_ratio = exp(median_diff))
sl_tests

plot_paired_diffs(sl_diffs, sl_tests,
                  x_lab = "Difference in mean log(step length + 1)",
                  title = "Step lengths") +
  facet_wrap(~ window, nrow = 1)

ggsave(paste0(outputs_dir, "paired_diff_step_length.png"),
       width = 250, height = 90, units = "mm", scale = 1, dpi = 600)

write_csv(sl_tests, paste0(outputs_dir, "paired_tests_step_length.csv"))

```

## Vegetation classes

Proportion of fixes in each vegetation class within each window. Positive differences mean the pig used that class more on the shoot day than 5 days before. Classes that a pig never used in either sequence contribute a difference of 0, so classes that are rarely used will have most of their differences at exactly 0.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 14

veg_diffs <- paired_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Veg_class)) %>%
  count(type, seq_id, name, window, Veg_class) %>%
  # fill classes that weren't used in a window with zeros, so the proportions are comparable
  complete(nesting(seq_id, name), type, window, Veg_class, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(type, seq_id, window) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.nan(prop)) %>%  # windows with no fixes
  select(-n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = prop) %>%
  mutate(diff = Observed - Pseudo,
         Veg_class = factor(Veg_class, levels = names(veg_colours))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff))

veg_tests <- paired_wilcox(veg_diffs, Veg_class, window)
veg_tests %>% arrange(p_value)

plot_paired_diffs(veg_diffs, veg_tests,
                  x_lab = "Difference in the proportion of fixes in each vegetation class",
                  title = "Vegetation classes") +
  facet_grid(Veg_class ~ window, labeller = labeller(Veg_class = label_wrap_gen(12))) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))

ggsave(paste0(outputs_dir, "paired_diff_veg_classes.png"),
       width = 250, height = 350, units = "mm", scale = 1, dpi = 600)

write_csv(veg_tests, paste0(outputs_dir, "paired_tests_veg_classes.csv"))

```
